chunks.heading: County business permits
chunks.text:
Obtain the county single business permit (SBP) for your trading location from the county government where the business operates. The SBP fee varies by county and business category. Some counties require additional sector-specific licences such as food handling or health permits.

The SBP must be displayed at the business premises. Operating without a valid permit may result in county enforcement action including fines or closure.

chunks.heading: Obtaining a KRA PIN
chunks.text:
After business registration, apply for a KRA PIN for the registered entity on iTax. The PIN application requires the certificate of registration, identification documents of directors or proprietors, and contact details. The PIN is required before opening a business bank account or registering for VAT.

Individual sole proprietors may use their personal PIN for the business if they operate under their own name, but a separate business PIN is recommended for clarity of tax records.

documents.title: Income Tax Basics for Small Business

chunks.heading: Income tax for small businesses
chunks.text:
Business income is taxed on profits after allowable business expenses. Resident companies pay corporation tax at 30% on taxable profits. Sole proprietors and partners are taxed at graduated individual rates on their share of business profit.

Taxable profit is gross business income less allowable business expenses. Allowable expenses include rent, salaries, utilities, stock purchases, depreciation of business assets, and other expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in producing income.

chunks.heading: Instalment tax
chunks.text:
Instalment tax applies where the estimated annual tax liability exceeds KES 40,000. Instalments are paid in four equal amounts by the 20th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the accounting year. Failure to pay instalments attracts interest.

Businesses should estimate annual profit early in the year and calculate expected tax to determine instalment obligations. Adjust estimates if business performance changes significantly.

Digital records including M-Pesa statements and eTIMS invoices are acceptable provided they are complete and accessible. Back up electronic records regularly.

Choosing between sole proprietorship and company registration depends on liability concerns, expected turnover, and access to contracts requiring corporate entities.

chunks.heading: Taxable, zero-rated and exempt supplies
chunks.text:
Taxable supplies are goods and services supplied in Kenya that attract VAT at the standard or zero rate. Standard-rated supplies attract VAT at 16%. Zero-rated supplies such as exports of goods and certain specified supplies are taxable at 0% and allow input VAT recovery on related purchases.

Exempt supplies do not attract VAT and the supplier cannot recover input VAT on purchases related to exempt supplies. Exempt supplies are excluded from the registration threshold calculation. Common exempt supplies include certain financial services, residential rent, and unprocessed agricultural produce as specified in the VAT Act.

chunks.heading: VAT registration threshold
chunks.text:

Registration is required within 30 days of exceeding the threshold. Voluntary registration is possible below the threshold if the person makes taxable supplies and wishes to recover input VAT.

chunks.heading: Eligibility for turnover tax
chunks.text:
Turnover tax applies to resident persons whose gross annual turnover exceeds KES 1,000,000 but does not exceed KES 25,000,000. Businesses with turnover below KES 1,000,000 may be exempt from TOT. Businesses with turnover above KES 25,000,000 must migrate to normal income tax and register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed the VAT threshold.

A person registered for VAT cannot be on turnover tax. A person on turnover tax who exceeds the upper band must notify KRA and migrate to the appropriate tax regime within the prescribed period.

chunks.text: Withholding tax returns are filed monthly on iTax by the 20th of the following month together with payment. The return must list each payee, payment type, gross amount, and WHT deducted. Annual reconciliation ensures all WHT certificates match declared payments.

chunks.heading: Credit notes and invoice corrections
chunks.text: Credit notes for returns, discounts, or corrections must also be generated through eTIMS. A credit note must reference the original invoice number and explain the reason for the adjustment. Both the original invoice and credit note are transmitted to KRA in real time.

chunks.heading: Electronic tax invoice requirements
chunks.text:
An electronic tax invoice must carry the seller name, address and KRA PIN, and the buyer PIN where the buyer is a registered person. It must include a unique invoice number, date and time of supply, and description of goods or services supplied.

Each line item must show quantity, unit price, and taxable value. The invoice must show the tax rate, VAT amount, and total amount payable. The eTIMS control number and QR code must appear on every invoice. Invoices without a valid eTIMS control number cannot be used to support input VAT claims by the buyer.

chunks.heading: Registering for eTIMS
chunks.text:
Businesses generate electronic tax invoices through eTIMS (Electronic Tax Invoice Management System). Onboarding is done through the eTIMS taxpayer portal using the KRA PIN and iTax credentials. All VAT-registered businesses and other persons required by KRA must register for eTIMS.

Sign up on the eTIMS taxpayer portal at the KRA website using your KRA PIN. Choose the eTIMS solution that fits your business: mobile app for small traders, client software integrated with a point-of-sale system, or the online portal for manual invoice generation.

Upload the required identification documents including certificate of registration or business name certificate and wait for KRA approval. Once approved, all invoices to other businesses must be generated through eTIMS. Paper invoices without eTIMS validation are not accepted for VAT purposes.

chunks.heading: eTIMS compliance and penalties
chunks.text: Failure to issue eTIMS-compliant invoices attracts penalties under the Tax Procedures Act. Businesses must ensure their eTIMS solution is connected and operational before making taxable supplies. Offline mode may be available for brief connectivity interruptions but invoices must be transmitted once connectivity is restored.

chunks.heading: eTIMS solutions for SMEs
chunks.text:
Small businesses may use the eTIMS mobile application available on Android and iOS. The mobile solution suits traders who issue a moderate number of invoices. Businesses with point-of-sale systems should integrate through certified eTIMS client software. The online portal suits businesses that issue invoices manually from a computer.

Each solution must be linked to the business KRA PIN. Only one active control unit per branch or trading location is permitted unless KRA approves otherwise.
